By the Cloud Architect:
1) In AWS Organizations, walk the account OU hierarchy against the target landing-zone model.
2) In AWS Organizations, review the service control policies attached at each OU tier.
3) In AWS VPC, review network segmentation and egress paths for the shared and workload accounts.
Done when in AWS Organizations every OU, guardrail and network segment has been reviewed against the target model.

By the Cloud Engineer:
1) In the AWS Console, attempt to deploy a deliberately non-compliant test resource (for example a public S3 bucket).
2) Confirm the service control policy denies the action.
3) Record the denied attempt and remove the test resource.
Done when in AWS the non-compliant deployment is denied by the guardrail.

By the Configuration Engineer:
1) In AWS IAM, confirm the provisioned roles exist and assume correctly.
2) In AWS VPC, check the required connectivity paths from the new account.
3) Flag any failed role assumption or blocked path.
Done when in AWS IAM the roles resolve and the connectivity paths succeed.

By the Infrastructure / Network Engineer:
1) In AWS Route 53, confirm the private hosted zone serves the endpoint records.
2) From an instance in each consuming AWS VPC subnet, resolve the endpoint name.
3) Confirm the answers return private IPs and record the results.
Done when in AWS Route 53 every consuming subnet resolves to the private endpoint.

By the Cloud Engineer:
1) Run the pipeline to apply the guardrail assignments.
2) In AWS Organizations, confirm the policies are attached across all target accounts.
3) Capture the apply output and the attachment listing.
Done when in AWS Organizations the guardrails show attached on every account.

By the Cloud Engineer:
1) Review CSPM scan results for buckets with public read or write access.
2) In AWS S3, confirm each flagged bucket's public access block and policy status.
3) Escalate confirmed exposures to SIEM/SOAR.
Done when in AWS S3 each flagged bucket is confirmed or cleared and no confirmed exposure lacks an alert.

By the Cloud Engineer:
1) Review CSPM findings for databases with public network access.
2) In AWS VPC, verify the database's security groups and subnet routing for public reachability.
3) Log confirmed findings to SIEM/SOAR.
Done when in AWS VPC each flagged database's exposure is verified and all confirmed exposures appear in SIEM/SOAR.

By the IAM Engineer:
1) In AWS IAM, review the applied policy on the remediated role.
2) Confirm wildcard and unnecessary admin grants are eliminated.
3) Document the final permission set.
Done when in AWS IAM the policy passes least-privilege review.
